summary: Round-1 minor 1 is resolved. In Order.attach (Order.java:777-781), an item that already has a seller keeps it. Only an item with no recorded owner takes al.sellerId(), and it falls back to PLATFORM_SELLER only when the allocation also has none. The allocation's sellerId cannot point at the wrong seller. ReservationService.reserve (ReservationService.java:199-208) sets it from the owner of the locked stock row (r.sellerId()). Those rows are found by product, variant and offer_id. Seller rows are always stored with their offerId (WarehouseService.java:143). The public seller write path checks that the caller owns the offer through SellerDirectory before writing (WarehouseService.java:100-106). Rows with no offer id belong to the platform. So the seller an allocation carries is the owner of that offer, or PLATFORM. Order.matches still accepts an allocation that has no offerId for any item of the same product and variant. In the worst case a seller's item could be booked to PLATFORM, never to another seller, and only for an order where one line has an offer and another line of the same product has none. That cannot happen because chooseOffer uses the same product view for both lines, and an item with no owner can only arise when offers.seller_id is null, which V7 forbids (NOT NULL). Old inventory nodes that send no sellerId behave as before (PLATFORM). The memoised SellerDirectory lookup is safe (InternalReservationController.java:80-96). The map is created fresh on each request, so nothing is shared across requests or threads. It is keyed only by offerId, and an offer has exactly one owner, so the cached owner is correct for every item with that offerId. An item that sends its own sellerId neither reads nor writes the cache. A 404 is cached as null, so the line still fails closed. An upstream error still becomes a 503 before the transaction opens. A cached owner paired with a different productId finds no rows and ends in a shortfall. Other changes in the delta: in WarehouseService, offerTotal now runs outside the publish try/catch, so a database error there fails the stock write instead of being logged. That is acceptable and has no security impact. The endpoints.md change only reorders the table and adds notes on known gaps; no new endpoint was added. The test changes add a write-vs-reserve concurrency check (rows never go negative, each successful reservation recorded once) and tighten the orphan and stale-offer tests. The diff adds no dependencies, secrets, PII, injection points or authorization changes. Round-1 minor 2 (inventory trusts a caller-supplied sellerId within the /internal/** trust model) is untouched by this delta and stays a backlog hardening item.
